$comment: The image models this repository's asset set is generated by, and where each one's set lives.
Read by BOTH providers.ts and providers.py. Two loaders reading one file cannot drift, and
four repositories reading the same SHAPE of file cannot fork.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY BYTE-IDENTICAL, checked with cmp rather than asserted. micro-brand's copy of
this file claims providers.py, compare.py and verify.py are byte-identical across the estate;
that claim is false and is being corrected there. compare.py is identical NOWHERE — the
difference is real logic, not a header line. So this file states only what a reader can check:
backends.ts, probe.ts   byte-identical to the sibling copies.
providers.ts, providers.py, replay.ts, dialects.json, dialects.py, dialects.ts,
materialise.py          byte-identical. These diverged briefly while the siblings gained the
prompt-dialect and set-switching machinery and this repository was
mid-run; the gap is now closed and every set here declares a dialect.
compare.py, verify.py,  deliberately different here, and each difference is named. verify.py
sheet.py,               carries a third ground class and two checks doc 23 section 2.15 asks
normalise_ground.py     for that nothing inherited; normalise_ground.py takes --provider
where the siblings are reference-only, which is what makes this the
one run in the estate whose ground-spread row is like-for-like; and
compare.py's inherited confound notes were false for this run.
Only verify.py's check_parity is genuinely shared, not the whole file.
The rule the estate actually wants is not sameness, it is that a DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE AND
SAID SO. An unexamined copy that has silently drifted is the thing to avoid, and asserting
sameness that stopped being true is how that happens.
LAYOUT. The reference provider's root is the repository itself: its assets are at assets/ and
its provenance is MANIFEST.json. That is a requirement rather than an aesthetic choice —
MANIFEST.json records a `path` for every entry, CI globs assets/**/*.png, and moving the
reference set to sets/flux/ to make the roots look alike would rewrite every one of those
paths in all four repositories.
So the challengers go under candidates/<id>/, which also states the truth: the reference set is
SHIPPED and a challenger is on trial. If a challenger wins it is promoted by moving its tree to
assets/, and the `provider` field on each entry records which model the shipped bytes came from.
ONE MANIFEST PER SET, not one merged manifest. Regenerating a candidate must never rewrite the
file that holds the reference set's provenance, and a candidate set is expected to be RED for
most of this exercise while the reference stays green. verify.py takes --provider and reads
exactly one manifest, so those two states do not collide.
$identity: How an asset is identified in THIS repository's manifests. The one thing that genuinely
differs between the estate's asset repositories: micro-brand keys on surface + kind, and the
three game sets key on a single dotted `asset` path such as objects/seating-stool.
Naming it here rather than in code is what keeps the LOADERS free of a hardcoded key, which
is what lets backends.ts and probe.ts be byte-identical across all four repositories and lets

providers.label: FLUX 2 Pro
providers.vendor: Black Forest Labs, served by Azure AI Foundry

billing.source: request_meta.cost on each response, recorded per asset as providerCostUnits

notes: Cost is NOT flat per image: 3 units up to roughly 1MP, 4.5 measured at 1920x768.
Delivered dimensions floor to a multiple of 16, which is why requestSizeFor rounds up.
Every declared size in this repository is already a multiple of 16 EXCEPT the two derived
title cards (1200x630 and 1600x900), which are cropped from compliant generations and
never requested. See docs/ecosystem/23-tessera.md §2.1.
Accepts no seed parameter, so `seed` is null on every entry rather than invented. That
absence is why Tessera authors ONE canonical facing per object and mirrors the second at
render time: a pipeline that cannot fix a seed cannot render the same chair four times.

providers.label: Qwen-Image 2512
providers.vendor: Alibaba Qwen, Azure AI Foundry Global Managed Compute

billing.basis: per hour the deployment exists, whether or not it generates anything

notes: THE MEASURED CONTRACT. Every line re-verified against the live endpoint rather than
taken on trust.
POST {FOUNDRY3_BASE_URL}/openai/v1/images/generations
api-key: <FOUNDRY3_API_KEY>            (Bearer is 401)
{"model":"qwen--qwen-image-2512","prompt":...,"response_format":"b64_json","n":1,"size":...}
1. It is NOT under /managed-deployments/. That route exists on a different host and is
what the earlier stub was written against; this is an OpenAI-shaped images route.
2. `response_format` is REQUIRED and must be b64_json. The default, url, is a 400 —
and that error is emitted by the model itself, which is how the route was found.
3. `width`/`height` are rejected outright: unrecognized_request_argument.
4. **`size` IS TRANSPOSED.** Asking for 1024x384 delivers a 384x1024 image while the
response still reports size 1024x384. Square sizes hide it completely, which is why a
1024x1024 probe looks correct. backends.ts compensates by sending height x width; that
is an envelope fix and touches nothing about the prompt.
THIS SET IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRECKED BY IT: 68 of the 288 generations are
non-square — 48 avatar plates at 256x512, 16 ward backdrops at 1536x640, and four wide
title assets. verify.py check 8 measures the delivered dimensions of every one of them
against the reference's, so the compensation is checked on the bytes rather than
trusted from the response, which reports the size it was asked for either way.
5. Exact sizes are honoured — no flooring to a multiple of 16, unlike the reference
provider. The round-up in requestSizeFor is kept anyway so a candidate produces the
same declared sizes as the reference and the two sets stay comparable asset for asset.
6. NO COST SIGNAL. background, quality and usage all come back null, so there is no
per-image figure to record and providerCostUnits stays null. Cost is deployment
hours; see COMPARISON.md section 6. It is never added to the reference's image units.
7. Measured ~15.4s per 1024x1024 image on the H100 this run held open.
8. The file size per megapixel is itself a signal, and it is the reason this set exists:
Qwen returned 7.1x the bytes per megapixel on micro-brand's FLAT vector brief against
2.6x on the painterly game sets. Tessera is painterly on purpose (doc 23 §1.1), so
this is the first brief in the estate that Qwen is not answering with the wrong idiom.

providers.label: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Super
providers.vendor: NVIDIA, Azure AI Foundry Global Managed Compute on A100_80GB

billing.basis: per hour the deployment exists, whether or not it generates anything

notes: WITHDRAWN, and carried across from the sibling repositories unchanged. The deployment
failed to come up on A100_80GB and has been deleted, so this is a placeholder rather than
a candidate: nothing runs against it and `present()` never returns it, because it has no
manifest.
It is KEPT, and kept complete, on purpose — and it matters more in THIS repository than in
the other three. doc 23 §1 states the constraint Tessera is built around: neither FLUX nor
Qwen emits a mesh, a UV layout, a rig or a frame of animation, so the whole title is
isometric 2D BECAUSE of what these two models cannot do. A third model is therefore a
question of when rather than if, and this entry is the seam it lands in.
deploymentVerified was set from a MEASUREMENT, not from the fact that it looked right.
The three answers that establish it, all with body {"model": "<name>"}:
nvidia--cosmos3-super          -> 400 BadRequestForDependentService (name resolves)
nvidia--cosmos-3-super         -> 404 DeploymentNotFound (the NATURAL spelling is wrong)
definitely--not--a--deployment -> 404 DeploymentNotFound (the control)
So a 400 that is not DeploymentNotFound means the gateway reached the model service and
the service rejected our body — which is the good state, and the reason probe.ts keys on
the error CODE rather than on the status.
Every env value above is read from the gitignored studio/.env.local. That file's key is
never written to this file, a manifest, a log line, a README or a report.
